facts.text: Director Rob Roy didn't just direct this one: he's also credited as writer, editor and cinematographer. A true one-person-band indie job.
A premiere write-up in The Hollywood Times pitches director Rob Roy's film as supernatural horror mixed with comedy and satire, with spiritual warfare and asylum madness thrown in.
The film was shot across three states: Virginia, Maryland and West Virginia. Heaven and Hell, apparently, share a regional commute.
The film's streaming rollout was announced for June 6, 2026 on Roku, Plex, Fawesome, Tubi and Prime Video channels, with Blu-ray releases promised too. Heaven goes ad-supported.
Director Rob Roy liked this world enough to return: a sequel, Damaged Disciples 2: Fallen Daughter, is already on his filmography.
Chaz Riddle plays a character named Reston Peace, and Autumn Fife pours drinks as the Pub Bartender. Even angels and demons need a bar.
Rob Roy's earlier credits include The Handler II - City Dog (2021) and a pandemic-era making-of with the gloriously long title 'what the f is a pandemic?'
Cast members Michelle Middleton, Stephanie Laurie, Lawrence Whitener and Russell Sage Patrick joined director Rob Roy for the film's premiere publicity photo.
TMDB tags this film with just four keywords: angel, social worker, demon, and good versus evil. Jimmy's day job is the wildest part of the pitch.
Databases file this one under adventure, fantasy and horror, a three-way genre mash for a movie about a social worker with no faith who ends up caught between angels and demons.
Hongmei Jian-Roy plays Origami in the film, and the cast list runs to about 17 credited players, many of them with colorfully named roles like Necro Dad and Crazed Nun.
Early praise cited by the film's publicity singles out its practical effects and atmospheric visuals, a fitting choice for an indie shot across three states on a shoestring.
Director Rob Roy's next listed project after this one is Lucid State, slated for 2026.
